div.head: Quadr Ded 4
div.ab: Opus enim, quod tuis exhortationibus et inconsulta, fateor, pollicitatione suscepi, maius est et creb[r]escentium cotidie malorum innouatione profusum exaggerationibus, permutationibus, permixturis, ex oppositis, ex adiunctis, rerum circumstanciis, contingentium modis.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 529 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

note.seg: vgl. u. 34; Hn 6, 2: noua nocendi fraus.
cf. below 34; Hn 6, 2: noua nocendi fraus.

Neuerungen beklagt Verf. öfter. S. u. 32. Dass hier solche im Strafrecht gemeint seien, ergibt der nächste Satz über Laster.—Die folg. Abstrakta dienen dem Vf., Rechtszustände zu beschreiben: Hn 22, 1

The author often complains of innovations. See below 32. That innovations in criminal law are meant here follows from the next sentence, on vices.—The abstract nouns that follow serve the author to describe legal conditions: Hn 22, 1

div.ab: For the work which I undertook at your exhortations and, I confess, by an ill-considered promise, is too great, and is spread out by the renewal of evils growing more frequent every day, by exaggerations, permutations, mixtures, from opposites, from adjuncts, by the circumstances of things, by the modes of contingent events.
